newsitem.title: USA: Davis ups Carter-Wallace bid to $20/shr.
newsitem.headline: Davis ups Carter-Wallace bid to $20/shr.

text.p: Billionaire investor Marvin Davis raised his bid for Carter-Wallace Inc, makers of Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorant, to $20 a share from his previous bid of $18 a share, a Davis spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said Davis sent a letter to Carter-Wallace chairman Henry Hoyt Jr and the company's board of directors on Friday notifying them of the sweetened bid.
She said she was not aware of any immediate response from Carter-Wallace.
A spokesman for Carter-Wallace said the company had "no comment at this point" to the latest Davis bid.

Based on Carter-Wallace's 46.39 million shares outstanding, the sweetened offer from the financier's Los Angeles-based Davis Companies was valued at $928 million, up from the original price of $835 million.
The Carter-Wallace takeover drive began on October 30 when New York-based Carter-Wallace said it had received the $18 a share bid from Davis.
Two days later, Carter-Wallace's majority shareholder, CPI Development Corp, said it had "no interest" in selling its shares for $18 each.

At that point, Davis responded saying an independent committee should be formed to determine whether the Davis bid was in the best interest of shareholders and said he would consider a higher bid "if one can be justified."
